title: Pricing the launch kit
scenario:
A sports-drink brand launches a new flavour. The client asks for a budget for the AI-made assets. The asset plan, the prices from Google's Gemini API pricing page and your team's own notes are in the exhibit.

All prices were copied on 2026-10-08.
exhibit:
Asset plan
  A. 40 social images, 1K, needed next Monday
  B. 4 hero images, 4K, needed this afternoon
  C. 6 video clips, 8 s each, 1080p, 9:16
  D. Voice-over for the clips, recorded in February 2027

Gemini API pricing page (checked 2026-10-08)
  Nano Banana 2.1, image output
    Standard: $30 per 1M tokens   Batch: $15 per 1M tokens
    1K image = 1,120 tokens   4K image = 3,780 tokens
    Free tier: not available
  Veo 3.1 Standard, per second: $0.40 (720p, 1080p), $0.60 (4k)
  Veo 3.1 Fast, per second: $0.10 (720p), $0.12 (1080p), $0.30 (4k)
  Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, audio output
    $0.00225 per 10 s of audio through December 31, 2026
    $0.0045 per 10 s of audio starting January 1, 2027

Gemini Batch API docs
  50% of the standard cost, 24-hour target turnaround

Team notes (ours, from the last campaign)
  Video: about 3 tries for every clip we keep

questions.prompt: What does one 4K hero image (item B) cost at the Standard rate?

options.text: $0.0336, because every Nano Banana 2.1 image costs the same.
options.explanation: That is the 1K price. The size step changes the token count: a 4K image uses 3,780 tokens, not 1,120.
Right. Tokens per image × price per token. Google's pricing page rounds it to $0.113 per 4K image.
That is the Batch price for a 4K image. Batch has a 24-hour target turnaround, and item B is needed this afternoon.

options.text: $30, the price shown on the pricing page.
options.explanation: $30 is the price for 1 million output tokens, not for one image. One 4K image uses 3,780 tokens.

questions.prompt: You plan item C on Veo 3.1 Fast at 1080p. Using the team note, what should you budget for the 6 kept clips?

options.explanation: This prices only the kept clips. The team note says about 3 tries for every clip you keep, so the budget must cover the tries too.
Right. Cost per try × tries per keeper × clips. The 3-tries figure is your team's own note, so check it on a small test.
$0.40 per second is the rate for Veo 3.1 Standard. The plan uses Veo 3.1 Fast, which is $0.12 per second at 1080p.
That is the cost of one kept clip. The plan needs 6 clips.

questions.prompt: How can you cut the cost of the 40 social images (item A) without changing their size?

options.text: Run them through the Batch API this week.
options.explanation: Right. Batch costs 50% of the standard rate ($0.0168 per 1K image, not $0.0336). Its 24-hour target fits a Monday deadline.

options.text: Use the free tier for them.
options.explanation: The pricing page lists the free tier for Nano Banana 2.1 as not available.

options.text: Make them at 4K, then shrink them to 1K.
options.explanation: A 4K image uses 3,780 tokens and a 1K image 1,120. Making them at 4K costs more, not less.

options.text: Make them at the Standard rate right away, so the team can review sooner.
options.explanation: That does not cut the cost. Standard is $0.0336 per 1K image, double the Batch price, and the images are not needed until Monday.

questions.prompt: For the voice-over (item D), a teammate prices 6 minutes of audio at $0.00225 per 10 seconds. What is wrong?

options.text: Nothing. Prices on the pricing page are fixed.
options.explanation: The page itself lists a new price that starts on January 1, 2027.

options.text: The rate is for text input, not audio output.
options.explanation: The exhibit lists $0.00225 per 10 s as the audio output price. The problem is the date, not the kind of token.

options.text: The recording is in 2027, so use $0.0045 per 10 seconds, double the teammate's.
options.explanation: Right. The page lists $0.00225 only through December 31, 2026. Write the date next to every price you quote.

options.text: Voice-over is billed per minute of audio, like transcription, so the rate is wrong.
options.explanation: OpenAI's pricing page shows a per-minute cost for gpt-transcribe. The exhibit shows this TTS model's price per 10 seconds of audio.
